newsitem.title: UK: LME copper touches fresh high, holds above $2,500.
newsitem.headline: LME copper touches fresh high, holds above $2,500.

text.p: LME copper notched up a fresh peak above the psychological $2,500 per tonne mark in early pre-market activity on Wednesday, but traders expected a modest retracement after Tuesday's fund-led $50 rally.
Three months copper surged to $2,513 but drifted back to $2,505, up from a previous kerb close of $2,493.

"There was a little bit of buying early on, but after that kind of rally I wouldn't be surprised to see it retrace to $2,500 or $2,490. It could even go down to $2,470 and not hurt the rally," one trader said.
Chartists said the market was overbought with an RSI of 76, which could inhibit the upside.
Stocks fell by 1,125 tonnes, more than the disappointing 475 tonnes on Tuesday, but less than some had expected.
The cash/threes backwardation was slightly wider at $78/$83 compared with $70/$75 at Tuesday's close.
Aluminium was looking soggy, however, having broken out of its recent range on Tuesday.
Prices took a stab higher early on Wednesday, skipping back above the key $1,650 area to $1,655, but quickly eased back to be last indicated at $1,645/48.
A decline in stocks of 2,400 tonnes -- after Tuesday's rise of 2,050 tonnes -- failed to raise the market.
Most analysts were convinced the market needed to explore the downside further, towards support at $1,637 or $1,616.
Zinc tried higher after Tuesday's strong performance, which came within a whisker of its recent high of $1,358.
Prices touched $1,356, up $3, before selling came in, reckoned to be of Chinese origin. Prices were last indicated at $1,350/52.
If prices broke above the recent peak, they might surge to $1,370/80, broker Rudolf Wolff said.

"However, with increasing concerns being voiced about the potential for Chinese material being delivered in the LME's Singapore warehouse, we would look to run close stops," Wolff analyst Martin Squires said.
On Wednesday, stocks fell by 1,525 tonnes.
Nickel also appeared vulnerable to further losses after diving by $165 on Tuesday.
Prices were indicated at $7,675/85, compared to Tuesday's $7,690, but were expected to attempt to fill the rest of a chart gap down to $7,620.
The market partially filled the gap on Tuesday, hitting a low of $7,650.
Lead was barely firmer at $625, up $2, and tin was little changed at $5,800, up $10.
Alloy was indicated unchanged at $1,500/10.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
